newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRENCH AND DUTCH RENEW EURO 96 ACQUAINTANCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRENCH AND DUTCH RENEW EURO 96 ACQUAINTANCE.

text.p: France coach Aime Jacquet takes another bold step towards building a World Cup-winning side by fielding two bright new hopes in a friendly international against the Netherlands on Wednesday.
Jacquet, his hand forced by injury to captain and key midfielder Didier Dechamps, is throwing Arsenal's Patrick Vieira in at the deep end with a debut on his first call to the squad.
"I'm not worried. He'll be well accompanied and in any case Patrick has a lot behind him," said Jacquet referring to the former Milan player's experience at under-21 level.
"I'm doing this without fears," said Jacquet, who also gives Bordeaux's exciting playmaker Ibrahim Ba a second successive outing after his brilliant debut against Portugal last month.
The last time the two countries met, at the European championship in June, France eliminated the Netherlands in a quarter-final that went to penalties.
"Evidently, the absence of Youri Djorkaeff, the loss of Deschamps and possibly also Zinedine Zidane have posed problems," Jacquet said.
"I have solutions available to do something else and I must profit from the sole advantage of our position (of not, as the next hosts, having to play World Cup qualifying games)."
Deschamps' Juventus team mate Zidane is in the side but faces a last minute fitness test on Wednesday, while Djorkaeff was allowed to put club duty for Internazionale Milan first.

Jacquet said Deschamps had a nagging calf problem. "He's already had two or three alerts, notably against Portugal and he missed his next club match. I think it's logical and normal to let him rest and not commit irreparable (damage)."
Deschamps is out for the first time since missing the Euro 96 semifinal penalty shoot-out loss to the Czech Republic.

The new-look midfield which also includes Pierre Laigle alongside his Sampdoria team mate Christian Karembeu will be backed by Jacquet's first string defence, the same five of Euro 96 including goalkeeper Bernard Lama.
Athletic Bilbao's left back Bixente Lizarazu returns from injury for his first international since August against Mexico.

Jacquet's side will be looking to confirm the fine form of their 2-0 away win over Portugal in Braga, a brilliant response to a poor performance in Denmark in December when they lost for the first time in 30 games.
France at home should prove a demanding exercise for the Dutch, who have swept to the top of European group seven in the World Cup qualifiers.
"The players must confirm that we are on the right track," temporary Dutch coach Jan Rab said.
Rab, standing in for Guus Hiddinck who underwent intestinal surgery recently and is still convalescent, said there would be no surprises in the Dutch side.
"Tactically, we might bring in a few slight changes, but as for the line-up, we have few surprises up our sleeve," he said.

The team should look much the same as that which crushed Belgium 3-0 away in their last qualifier in December, although without midfielder Aron Winter who like Djorkaeff will be with Inter for their Italian Cup semifinal at Napoli.
But perhaps in the wake of Ajax Amsterdam's encouraging return to form in a 3-0 win over Feyenoord at the weekend, there might be a starting place for striker Patrick Kluivert.
Teams:

France - 1-Bernard Lama; 15-Lilian Thuram, 5-Laurent Blanc, 8-Marcel Desailly, 3-Bixente Lizarazu; 19-Christian Karembeu, 12-Pierre Laigle, 6-Patrick Vieira, 13-Ibrahim Ba; 10-Zinedine Zidane, 11-Christophe Dugarry.

Netherlands (probable) - 1-Edwin van der Sar; 2-Michael Reisiger, 4-Frank de Boer, 5-Arthur Numan, 3-Jaap Stam; 8-Ronald de Boer, 6-Wim Jonk, 10-Clarence Seedorf, 11-Philip Cocu; 9-Dennis Bergkamp, 14-Marc Overmars.
